subject.title: Feature Request: Add .gitignore-like exclude patterns to backup CLI

question: Should OpenClaw add native backup exclude-pattern controls now, and which defaults, protected paths, and exclude-file behavior should become part of the core CLI contract?
rationale: The missing capability is source-reproducible, but defaults and protected recovery paths decide the balance between backup size, sensitive-file avoidance, and restorable archives.

options.title: Review linked PR as canonical
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a narrowed replacement to settle defaults, protected paths, manifest/JSON compatibility, and proof before landing.

options.title: Start with explicit custom excludes
options.body: Accept `--exclude` and `--exclude-file` first while deferring smart defaults and implicit ignore loading until restore completeness and security expectations are clearer.

options.title: Defer native excludes
options.body: Keep core backups coarse, document the current scope, and direct optional backup strategies to plugin or ClawHub paths after an explicit maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Review linked PR as canonical
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a narrowed replacement to settle defaults, protected paths, manifest/JSON compatibility, and proof before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: gumadeiras is tied to the original backup CLI review and current backup infra extraction, making them the strongest code-history owner for this policy choice.
